```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Read the data

```{r}
# Read in soil core dataset
soil_cores <- read_csv(here("eds222-recorded-lectures","data","exide-soil-cores.csv")) |> 
    # Filtering out outliers for visualization purposes
    filter(pb_ppm <= 5000)

# Samples from the expanded areas
ena_esa <- soil_cores |> 
    # Create an "area" column
    mutate(area = str_sub(property_id, 1, 3)) |> 
    # Keep only the rows in the expanded area
    filter(area %in% c("ENA","ESA")) |> 
    # Slice a smaller sample (for visualization purposes)
    slice_sample(n = 40, by = area)
```

## Visualize the Data

First, let's visualize the data. With a categorical predictor, _jitter_ the x-axis so the points don't overlap.

```{r}
ggplot(ena_esa, aes(area, pb_ppm)) +
    geom_point(
        shape = 21,
        fill = "cornflowerblue",
        color = "white",
        alpha = 0.5,
        # Jitter the points left-to-right for easier visualization
        position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 222)
    )
```

## Fit the Model

Now, fit the model with `lm()`.

```{r}
# The formula is the same whether the predictor is continuous or categorical
ena_esa_lm <- lm(pb_ppm ~ area, data = ena_esa)
```

## Generate Summary

Use `summary()` to see the coefficients and other properties of the model.

```{r}
summary(ena_esa_lm)
```

## Summary Interpretation:

`(Intercept)`: mean pb_ppm ENA group (beta0)
`areaESA`: DIFFERENCE between mean pb_ppm ENA and mean pb_ppm ESA (beta1)
- So, mean pb_ppm ESA (beta0+beta1) is `(Intercept)` + `areaESA`
